contradictions.fact: Standard descent: rappel the face or not

claims.says: The published route description gives the standard descent as rappelling the face directly — 5-6 rappels using two ropes ... walk off the standard gully descent back toward the Hairpin Turn (roughly 2 hours), which avoids needing a second rope at all
Do not plan to rappel the Beckey-Tate line itself ... most parties explicitly avoid it
Optional: 5-6 rappels with two ropes from anchored stations, but the loose rock and awkward angles make the walk-off gully the preferred descent.
Two single-rope (60m) rappels from slung-block anchors at successive notches, or a scree-and-snow gully walk-off

contradictions.why: The rope note calls rappelling the face the standard descent and the gully a no-rappel walk-off, while the descent fields tell parties not to rappel the face and put two rappels in the gully descent.
contradictions.internal_resolution: descent, descent_text, rappels, bail and itinerary all make the notch/gully descent (with two single-rope rappels) standard; rope_note is the outlier
